article_lead.description: the part of EM that converts probabilities for missing data into updated model parameters by maximizing a weighted likelihood

new_bank_questions.title: Fixed weights during the M step
new_bank_questions.body: When maximizing Q(Psi;Psi_old) for a mixture, are the responsibilities recomputed for each candidate Psi? Explain.
new_bank_questions.answer: No. The E step computed responsibilities using Psi_old; they stay fixed while the M step varies candidate Psi. The next E step recomputes them after the parameter update.

new_bank_questions.title: Zero effective component count
new_bank_questions.body: A mixture component has effective count N_h=0 after the E step. What fails in the usual weighted-mean M-step update?
new_bank_questions.answer: Its denominator is zero, so the mean is undefined by that formula. A fitting procedure must handle the boundary or alter initialization or constraints.

new_bank_questions.title: Two-point mixture M step
new_bank_questions.body: For x=(0,2), the component-one E-step responsibilities are (0.75,0.25). Find both updated weights and both updated means, with variances fixed.
new_bank_questions.answer: Effective counts are 1 and 1, so weights are 0.5 and 0.5. The weighted means are 0.5 for component one and 1.5 for component two.
